primary_title: Student Generative AI Survey 2025 (HEPI Policy Note 61)
date_evidence: HEPI's own publication page shows 26 February 2025 and links the PDF (hepi.ac.uk/wp-content/uploads/2025/02/HEPI-Kortext-Student-Generative-AI-Survey-2025.pdf).
notes: Page gives 88% using AI for assessments (92% any AI); speaker's 90% is a rounding.

primary_title: Artificial Intelligence sector study 2024
primary_publisher: Department for Science, Innovation and Technology
date_evidence: gov.uk page header: 'Published 3 September 2025'.
notes: The 2024 study says 'Ninety-five percent of companies identified in 2024 are SMEs (2023 = 96%)'. The 2025 study (gov.uk, 'Published 29 October 2026', the debate day) says 'Ninety-six percent of companies identified in 2025 were SMEs', so the 96% matches the 2025 edition even though the speaker named the 2024 study.

primary_title: Elon Musk post on Twitter/X ('Worth reading Superintelligence by Bostrom... Potentially more dangerous than nukes')
date_evidence: No primary tweet page found; the 3 August 2014 date comes only from news coverage (Business Insider, CS Monitor 4 Aug 2014) in search results.
notes: Wording is clearly the August 2014 tweet; the same line is also used as a blurb on Bostrom's book listings. The tweet itself was not located in searches.

primary_title: Lord Speaker's Lectures listing: Professor Stuart Russell lecture on artificial intelligence
date_evidence: Search snippet of the parliament.uk Lord Speaker's Lectures page: 'On 18 October 2022, the professor of computer science at the University of California, Berkeley, delivered a lecture on the subject of artificial intelligence.' (host not reachable from this session).
notes: No transcript or video found. The title 'AI: Promise and Peril' comes from Lord McFall's PoliticsHome piece, not from a parliament.uk page. The speaker's 'Stanford' is wrong; Russell is at Berkeley.

primary_title: Statement on AI Risk (press release: 'AI Extinction Statement')
date_evidence: Press release reads 'For immediate release: May 30, 2023'; it links the statement itself at https://www.safe.ai/statement-on-ai-risk (not opened).
notes: Statement text matches the speaker's paraphrase.

primary_title: AI and Eating Disorders: How generative AI enables and promotes harmful eating disorder content
primary_publisher: Center for Countering Digital Hate (site now titled Center for Countering Digital Harm)
date_evidence: The CCDH report page (counterhate.com URL 308-redirects to counterharm.com) shows publication date 7 August 2023; the PDF filename is dated 230705 and the prompts were run in June 2023.
notes: This is the 2023 baseline. The 'recent' comparison report is not clearly identified; no 2026 CCDH eating-disorder report was found, so Fake Friend (Aug 2025) is the likely one.

primary_title: Gen-AI: Artificial Intelligence and the Future of Work (Staff Discussion Note SDN/2024/001)
date_evidence: IMF publication page gives 'January 14, 2024'; the note's PDF text (sdnea2024001) says the UK has 'almost 70 percent of employment ... in high-exposure occupations'.
notes: DSIT's January 2026 'Assessment of AI capabilities and the impact on the UK labour market' uses the same 'around 70% of UK workers' wording (35% high/high complementarity), so the speaker may have taken it from there. The IMF's 2026 UK Article IV says 'nearly two-thirds', which does not match the speaker.

primary_title: Regulation (EU) 2024/1689 (Artificial Intelligence Act), Article 50
primary_publisher: European Parliament and Council of the EU (EUR-Lex)
date_evidence: EUR-Lex text opened: title 'Regulation (EU) 2024/1689 ... of 13 June 2024'; Official Journal header 'OJ L, 2024/1689, 12.7.2024'. Art. 50(2) (machine-readable marking) and 50(4) (deep fake disclosure) confirmed in the text.
notes: The coder's date is the OJ publication date (adoption was 13 June 2024; entry into force 1 Aug 2024; Art. 50 applies from 2 Aug 2026, though I did not read Art. 113 on the page). 'Framework' may also cover the Commission's 2026 code of practice on marking AI-generated content and Digital Omnibus changes.

primary_title: Regulation (EU) 2024/1689 (Artificial Intelligence Act), Article 55(1)(c)
primary_publisher: European Parliament and Council of the EU (EUR-Lex)
date_evidence: EUR-Lex text opened: title 'Regulation (EU) 2024/1689 ... of 13 June 2024'; Official Journal header 'OJ L, 2024/1689, 12.7.2024'. Art. 55(1)(c): providers of GPAI models with systemic risk must 'keep track of, document, and report, without undue delay, to the AI Office' serious incidents.
notes: Coder's '2024-07' is the OJ month; the act is dated 13 June 2024. The Art. 55 duties apply from 2 Aug 2025.

primary_title: AEC Opening Statement, Senate Select Committee on Adopting Artificial Intelligence (AI), 20 May 2024
date_evidence: PDF heading reads 'Opening Statement Senate Select Committee on Adopting Artificial Intelligence (AI), 20 May 2024'; PDF creation date is also 2024-05-20.
notes: The hearing was 20 May 2024; the coder's 21 May is the news date. The statement says the AEC cannot deter or detect false AI content. The 'expect AI disinformation' wording was in oral evidence (Committee Hansard 20 May 2024, p.27, per the committee report), and I did not find that transcript. The AEC may have repeated the warning later.

primary_title: Regulation (EU) 2024/1689 (Artificial Intelligence Act)
primary_publisher: European Parliament and Council of the EU (EUR-Lex)
date_evidence: EUR-Lex text opened: title 'Regulation (EU) 2024/1689 ... of 13 June 2024'; Official Journal header 'OJ L, 2024/1689, 12.7.2024'.
notes: Coder's date is the OJ publication date; adoption was 13 June 2024 and entry into force 1 Aug 2024.

primary_title: Senate Standing Committee Opening Statement: Criminal Code Amendment (Deepfake Sexual Material) Bill 2024
date_evidence: Search snippet dates the opening statement 23 July 2024, with the text 'increased ... as much as 550 per cent year on year since 2019'; the eSafety site returned 503.
notes: eSafety's August 2024 submission (esafety.gov.au/sites/default/files/2024-08/..., seen in search, 503) describes it as a 550% rise between 2019 and 2023, which is cumulative, not year on year. The figure is third-party data, and eSafety may have repeated it later.

primary_title: Regulation (EU) 2024/1689 (Artificial Intelligence Act)
primary_publisher: European Parliament and Council of the EU (EUR-Lex)
date_evidence: EUR-Lex text opened: title 'Regulation (EU) 2024/1689 ... of 13 June 2024'; Official Journal header 'OJ L, 2024/1689, 12.7.2024'. Art. 55(1)(c) incident reporting confirmed in the text.
notes: Coder's date is the OJ publication date. The claim also covers California SB 53 and New York's RAISE Act, which were not checked.

primary_title: UK General Election news and opinion-formation survey 2024
date_evidence: Search result title of the Ofcom PDF reads 'Report Published 10 September 2024'; the fetch returned 403.
notes: Search snippet confirms 57% concerned, 46% did not know whether they had seen a deepfake, and 27% saw one in the previous week, matching all three of the speaker's figures.

primary_title: Report on the 2024 UK Parliamentary general election and the May 2024 elections
date_evidence: The PDF sits in the site's 2024-11 upload folder (search result); the report page returned 403, so no day was seen.
notes: Search snippet: 'around one in four people (24%) said they saw or heard a deepfake'. The speaker calls it 'recent'; the Commission repeated the figure in later evidence to Parliament (SMH0021, not opened) and has a 2026 tracker.

primary_title: Supplemental Meta Platforms Technologies Terms of Service
date_evidence: Page reads 'Last updated: April 29, 2025'; s.2.1 puts on the user 'obtaining any consents from other individuals who you interact with on your MPT Products'.
notes: The AI-training language is in the UK Supplemental MPT Privacy Policy (meta.com/gb/legal/privacy-policy/, opened), which is 'Effective from 12 October 2026'. If the speaker meant the terms in force on 4 Nov 2026, the source is under a month old, not 18.7 months.

primary_title: Macroeconomic productivity gains from Artificial Intelligence in G7 economies (OECD Artificial Intelligence Papers No. 41)
date_evidence: The OECD page returned 403; the RePEc/EconPapers record (opened) dates the paper 2025-06-30 and quotes the abstract's '0.4-1.3 percentage points' range.
notes: I did not open the Budget 2026 document to confirm which OECD source it cites.

primary_title: Me, Myself and AI: Understanding and safeguarding children's use of AI chatbots
date_evidence: The PDF is in the 2025/07 upload folder and search results describe a July 2025 publication; the PDF and press release returned 403.
notes: Search snippet: '12% ... no one else to speak to, which rises to nearly one in four (23%) vulnerable children'. Coverage dated about 13-15 July 2025.

primary_title: Fake Friend: How ChatGPT betrays vulnerable teens by encouraging dangerous behavior
primary_publisher: Center for Countering Digital Hate (site now titled Center for Countering Digital Harm)
date_evidence: The CCDH report page (counterhate.com URL 308-redirects here) shows publication date 6 August 2025.
notes: The page lists 'restrictive diet plans' at 20 minutes and hiding eating habits from family at 25 minutes, matching the speaker's 'within 20 minutes'. A republished PDF is dated 12 Sep 2025. No newer CCDH eating-disorder report was found.

primary_title: Artificial Intelligence sector study 2024
primary_publisher: Department for Science, Innovation and Technology
date_evidence: gov.uk page header: 'Published 3 September 2025'; text: 'Almost 90% of AI business representatives surveyed expect revenues to grow within the next 12 months'.
notes: The 2025 edition (published 29 Oct 2026) does not appear to contain this figure, which supports the 2024 study as the source.

primary_title: eSafety moves against services used to 'nudify' Australian school children (media release)
date_evidence: The release returned 503. An eSafety document set (esafety.gov.au/sites/default/files/2026-04/LOG_187_Document_Set.pdf, seen in search) gives the formal warning as issued 2 September 2025, about 100,000 monthly Australian visits; this is the date of the action, not confirmed as the release date.
notes: A follow-up eSafety release (November 2025) says the provider then withdrew from Australia; 'took action in 2025' fits either release.
